heroHeadline: CJP fractures: rebel volunteer launches CJP-Democratic, accusing founder Dipke of ceding leadership to AAP
heroSubtitle: The movement's first major internal split emerged Sep 3 when former volunteer Manish Brahmbhatt launched a breakaway Cockroach Janata Party-Democratic (CJP-D), alleging that after the Jantar Mantar success 8 of 12 seats on CJP's national committee went to people with Aam Aadmi Party ties and that leadership travel was sponsored through informal networks linked to Arvind Kejriwal, with no volunteer or protester consulted. Founder Abhijeet Dipke rejected the 'B team' framing the same day, insisting the organisation answers only to students. The Jharkhand, Bihar and campus-admissions fronts remain unchanged since their early-September concessions, and the CJP's planned Sept 5 return march stays called off following the Supreme Court's Sep 1 order quashing FIRs against NEET protesters.
